title: If Your Car Could Drive Straight Up, Space Is an Hour Away

scenes.text: If your car could drive straight up, you'd reach space in an hour.
Space officially begins about 100 kilometers up. At highway speed, that is a sixty minute drive.
The nearest big city is probably farther from you right now than space is.
It's that close because the air thins out fast. Up there, it's too thin for a wing to hold up a plane.
So space isn't far. It's just straight up. An hour's drive, with no road.

description:
If your car could drive straight up, you'd reach space in about an hour.
The internationally used edge of space, the Karman line, sits about 100 kilometres (62 miles) above sea level; NASA and the US Air Force use 80 kilometres (50 miles). Either way, space is closer than the next big city.
Where would you drive to first if roads went straight up?
thumbnail_text: SPACE IS AN HOUR'S DRIVE AWAY
first_comment: Space is 100 km up. How far is the nearest big city from you? Bet it's farther.
